## Purpose
Changing a saved workflow by instruction (Refine with AI). These routes propose a revision, review it, apply or discard it, and manage the version history: list, restore and undo.

## Responsibilities
| Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET /workflows/{name}/revisions` | `{"revisions": [...]}`, oldest first (the conversation) |
| `POST /workflows/{name}/revisions` (201) | propose a change |
| `GET /workflows/{name}/revisions/{id}` | one proposal |
| `POST /workflows/{name}/revisions/{id}/apply` | apply it; 409 when the workflow has changed since |
| `POST .../discard` | reject it |
| `GET /workflows/{name}/revision-suggestions` | one-click prompts built from validation issues |
| `GET /workflows/{name}/versions` and `/versions/{no}` | saved states, newest first |
| `POST /workflows/{name}/versions/{no}/restore` | restore a state, recorded as a new version |
| `POST /workflows/{name}/undo` | go back to the previous state |

- **Propose body (`ProposeRevisionRequest`):**
  - `instruction`, at most 4000 characters;
  - `focus_step_ids`, at most 50;
  - `operations`, at most 25; an edit chosen in the UI, which skips interpreting an instruction;
  - `origin`: `editor` or `planner`.
- **Apply body (`ApplyRevisionRequest`):** `{allow_errors: False}`. Set it to true to keep a change that leaves the workflow with errors.

## Key elements
Every service call is wrapped so that a `RevisionError` becomes an `HTTPException` with the error's own `status_code` and message.

## Control flow
Proposing never changes the workflow. Applying and restoring do, and each records a version first.

## Data, state and side effects
Through `services/workflow_revision_service.py`: the revision and version tables and the workflow records. Proposing calls Mistral.

## Configuration
`WORKFLOW_MAX_VERSIONS` limits the history that is kept.

## Interactions
- Route policy: `/workflows` GET needs workflows.view; writes need workflows.manage.
- Used by the frontend builder's Refine panel and its history.

## Error handling and edge cases
The status codes come from `RevisionError`.

## Nuances and gotchas
Publishing is separate (`POST /workflows/{name}/publish`). A revised workflow goes live only when the user publishes it.

## How to rebuild this file
Ten thin handlers delegating to the revision service, plus the two body models.

## Tests
`backend/tests/test_workflow_revisions.py` and `test_rebuild_and_refine.py`.
